key_insight: Boron nitride nanotubes host multiple room-temperature single-photon emitters at different visible wavelengths within one compact structure.
engineering_relevance: With radii of approximately 25 nm, these nanotubes offer a compact platform for potential integration into quantum-photonic waveguides and interferometric filters.
method: Locate and characterize emitters using confocal photoluminescence microscopy.
Assess single-photon emission using Hanbury Brown–Twiss interferometry.
Apply surface passivation or coatings to reduce blinking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports emitters across the visible spectrum, lifetimes as short as 0.5 ns—about twice as fast as the fastest hBN emitters—and reduced blinking after surface treatment.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify photon purity, device yield, or long-term stability, and deterministic photonic integration remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
